_meta.purpose: Jira Automation rule config for the D4/Sec. 4.4 trigger integration -- import-assisted, not hand-reconstructed from prose.
_meta.schema_note: Modeled on Atlassian's own 'Export rule' JSON shape for Automation for Jira (Cloud). Atlassian does not publish this export format as a stable, versioned public schema, so a human importing this MUST verify it imports cleanly in their org's Jira instance (Project settings -> Automation -> ... -> Import rule) and adjust field names if their Jira Cloud version has drifted from this shape. If import fails, SETUP.md gives the exact manual click-through steps to reconstruct this rule by hand from the values below -- the values (trigger status, opt-in label, target URL, headers) are the authoritative part; the exact JSON envelope around them is best-effort.

rule.name: SDLC Auto: dispatch opted-in story on trigger-status transition
rule.description: Fires when a story enters the team's existing 'queued and ready to start' status AND carries the ai-factory opt-in label. Sends an unsigned (TLS-only) web request to D4's webhook relay, which independently re-verifies the opt-in label via get-issue, computes the Sec. 17.3 per-tenant HMAC signature, and forwards a signed dispatch to D1's job-dispatcher endpoint. See services/issue-tracker/SETUP.md for why this extra hop exists (native Jira Automation cannot compute an HMAC signature at send-time).

value.description: Issue transitioned (any transition; the CONDITION below narrows to the specific target status).
Status matches the configured trigger status AND the opt-in label is present. Both must hold -- being in the trigger status alone is never sufficient (master spec Sec. 4.4).

Send a web request to D4's webhook relay (see webhook_relay.py) -- not directly to D1 -- because the relay is what computes the real Sec. 17.3 HMAC signature D1 verifies; Jira Automation's native action cannot compute that signature itself.
